spans.s:
कत कत, अस्, m. the clearing nut plant;
see the following; N. of a Muni or saint.
—कत-
फल, अस्, m. the clearing nut plant.

कतक, अस्, m. the clearing nut plant, Strychnos
Potatorum, (one of the seeds of this plant being rubbed
upon the inside of the water-jars used in Bengal occa-
sions a precipitation of the earthly particles diffused
through the water and removes them.)

कतम कतम, अस्, आ, अत् (superlative of 2. क;
declined as a pronom.,
Gram. 236

), who or which of
many ? (e. g. कतमेन पथा यातास् ते, by which
road have they gone?). कतम is often a mere
strengthened substitute for क, the superlative affix
imparting emphasis. Hence it may occasionally be
used for ‘who or which of two?’ (e. g. तयोः कत-
मस्मै, to which of these two ?). It may option-
ally be compounded with the word to which it refers
(e. g. कतमः कठः or कतम-कठः, which
Kaṭha out of many?). When followed by च and
preceded by यतम an indefinite expression is
formed equivalent to ‘any whosoever,’ ‘any whatso-
ever,’ &c. (e. g. यतमद् एव कतमच् च विद्यात्,
he may know anything whatsoever). In negative
sentences कतम with चन or कतम with अपि
= not even one, none at all (e. g. न कतमच्-
चनाहः, not even on a single day, on no day at
all). In addition to the above uses कतम is said to
mean ‘best,’ ‘excessively good-looking;’ [cf. 3. क.]
—कतमोरग (˚म-उर्˚), अस्, m., N. of a man.

कतर, अस्, आ, अत् (comparative of 2. क; declined
[]
as a pronom.,
Gram. 236

), who or which of two?
whether of two? Analogously to कतम above
कतर may occasionally be used to express ‘who or
which of many’ (e. g. कतरस्यां दिशि, in which
quarter ?), and may optionally be compounded with
the word to which it refers (e. g. कतरः कठः
or कतर-कठः). In negative sentences कतर
with चन = neither of the two (e. g. न कतरश्-
चन जिग्ये, neither of the two was conquered;
[cf. Gr. πότερος, κότερος; Goth. hvathar; Eng.
whether; Lat. uter; Old Germ. huedar; Slav.
kotoryi.]

कातर कातर, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. कतर?),
cowardly, discouraged, timid, depressed, perplexed,
shrinking, afraid; confused, agitated, disordered; (अस्),
m. a large kind of fish, Cyprinus Catla, = कातल.
—कातर-ता, f. or कातर-त्व, अम्, n. cowardice,
timidity, agitation.
कतरतस्, ind. on which of the two sides ?
1. कति (fr. 2. क, declined in pl. only,
Gram. 227

.
अ, all the cases except the nom. voc. and acc. taking
terminations, whereas the correlative इति has become
fixed as an indeclinable adverb), how many? quot?
several (e. g. कति देवाः, how many gods? कति
व्यापादयति कति वा ताडयति, some he kills and
some he strikes). In the sense of ‘several,’ ‘some,’
कति is generally followed by चिद् or अपि (e. g. कतिचिद्
अहानि, for several or some days). कति may be used
as an adverb with चिद् in the sense of ‘oftentimes,’
‘much,’ ‘in many ways’ (e. g. कतिचित् स्तुतः, much
or often praised). कति-कृत्वस्, ind. how many
times? कति-विध, अस्, आ, अम्, of how many kinds?
कति-शस्, how many at a time?

कति 2. कति, इस्, m., N. of a sage, son of
Viśvā-mitra and ancestor of Kātyāyana. (For 1. see
above.)

काति काति, इस्, इस्, इ (fr. 2. का = कन्), wishing,
desiring (in the compounds ऋण-काति and काम-
काति).

कतिथ, अस्, ई, अम्, to what place or stage or
degree advanced? (the how-maniest?) with चिद् =
advanced to such and such a point (e. g. अहं
कतिथश्चिद् आस, I was so far advanced on to such
and such a point).

कतिधा, ind. in how many places? in how many
parts? how often? कतिधा चित्, everywhere.

कतिपय, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (pl. m. ए and आस्),
several, some; a certain number, so many; कति-
पयेन अहर्गणेन, after some days; also कति-
पयैर् अहोभिः, कतिपयाहस्य, &c.
—कतिप-
येन or कतिपयात्, ind. with some exertion; [the
affix पय has been compared with Gr. ποῖος]

कतिपयथ, अस्, ई, अम्, advanced to a certain
place or degree.

कतमाल कतमाल, अस्, m. fire; the right
form is खतमाल; [cf. also कचमाल and कर-
माल.]
कतिक or कतिका, f., N. of a town.

कतीमुष कतीमुष, अम्, n., N. of an Agra-
hāra.

कत्ताशब्द कत्ता-शब्द, अस्, m. the rattling
sound of dice.

कत्तृण कत्-तृण, कत्-तोय, कत्-त्रि. See
under 2. कद्.

कातृण का-तृण, अम्, n. a species of grass,
Rohisha-tṛṇa; [cf. कत्-तृण.]

कत्थ् कत्थ्, cl. 1. A. कत्थते, -थितुम्,
to boast; to mention with praise, to praise
or celebrate; to flatter or coax; to abuse, revile.

कत्थन, अस्, आ, अम्, boasting, praising; a boaster,
praiser; (अम्), n. boasting.

कत्पय कत्-पय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 2. कद् and
पय fr. पी = प्यै), Ved. swelling, rising; (Sāy.)
one whose waters cause happiness.

कत्र् कत्र्, cl. 10. P. कत्रयति, -यितुम्, to
loosen, slacken, remove.

कत्सवर कत्सवर, अम्, n. the shoulder,
the shoulder-blade.

कातन्त्र का-तन्त्र, अम्, n. title of a grammar
(= कलाप, q. v.); there are several appendices to
and commentaries on this grammar, called कातन्त्र-
गणधातु, ˚चतुष्टयप्रदीप, ˚चन्द्रिका, ˚धा-
तुघोषा, &c.
—कातन्त्र-पञ्जिका, f. title of a
commentary by Trilocana-dāsa.
कातरायण, अस्, m. a patronymic fr. कातर.

कातर्य, अम्, n. timidity, fear, dejection, depres-
sion of spirits.

कातल कातल, अस्, m. a large kind of fish,
Cyprinus Catla; N. of a man; [cf. कातर.]
कातलायन, अस्, m. a patronymic fr. कातल.

कातीय कातीय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. कात्य below),
composed by Kātya (e. g. in कातीय-गृह्यसूत्र,
कातीय-कल्प-सूत्र, and कातीय-सूत्र); a N. of
Kātyāyana (?); a pupil of the same; also कात्या-
यनीय (?).

कात्य, अस्, m. a patronymic fr. कत; also = का-
त्यायन (?).

कात्यायन, अस्, m. (a patronymic fr. कति or
कात्य), N. of the author of several treatises on
ritual, grammar, &c.; he is generally identified with
Vararuci, the author of the Prākṛta-prakāśa. He is
also the author of the Vārttikas or supplementary
rules to Pāṇini, of the Yajur-veda Prātiśākhya, and
the Śrauta-sūtras; (ई), f., N. of one of the two wives
of Yājñavalkya; an epithet of Durgā; a middle-aged
widow dressed in red clothes.
—कात्यायन-सूत्र,
अम्, n. the Śrauta-sūtras of Kātyāyana.
—कात्यायन-
सूत्र-पद्धति, a commentary on the last by Yājñi-
ka-deva.
—कात्यायनसूत्र-भाष्य, अम्, n. a com-
mentary on the same by Karka.
—कात्यायनी-पुत्र,
अस्, m., N. of a teacher.
—कात्यायनी-माहात्म्य,
अम्, n. a part of the Skanda-purāṇa.
कात्यायन कात्यायन. See under कातीय.

कातु कातु, उस्, m. a cave; a well (?); [cf.
काट.]

कात्कृ कात्-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते,
-कर्तुम् (fr. कात्, an exclamation of abuse, and 1. कृ),
to insult, dishonour.
कात्-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, dishonoured, insulted.

कात्त्रेयक कात्त्रेयक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कत्-त्रि),
produced from or belonging to any combination of
three inferior articles.

कात्थक्य कात्थक्य, अस्, m. (a patronymic
fr. कत्थक), N. of a commentator.
